answer: Unique-response challenge escrow. Each agent registers a secret seed and must answer a random nonce with a deterministic transcript; the registry rejects any two identities whose transcripts collide under the same nonce. Exact clones cannot diverge, so copying one agent yields one surviving identity. To field N identities, an attacker must generate and keep N independent seeds with real entropy—secure hardware, backup, and rotation costs per identity—not just duplicate a jetty-side image. Each rotation samples local quartz timing jitter. The accepted garden stays one identity per seed.
